subject: Intermittent 503s + sustained latency in production — Zenith Health
messages:
From: Sara Patel <sara.patel@zenithhealth.com>
To: mateo_alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Reed <alex.reed@zenithhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2027 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Production errors and slowdowns — seeing 503s in batching job

Hey Mateo / Marissa,

We started seeing a spike in 503s and sustained tail latency on our nightly billing batch around 13:50 PT. The job is hitting Redwood's text-generation API and latency jumps from ~120ms to several seconds, with roughly 8–12% 503s for about 25 minutes. It looks correlated to an increase in concurrent worker count but this run is within the baselined QPS we've been on for the last 3 months.

Attached are traces from our side (zenith_request_traces_20270921.zip). Can you confirm whether anything changed in rate/ burst policy on Redwood's side this morning or if a global rate limiter could have been applied? This is impacting our reconciliation windows.

Appreciate urgency — our ops window is tight.

—Sara
Senior Platform Engineer
Zenith Health

[attachment: zenith_request_traces_20270921.zip (application/zip)]

From: mateo_alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>

Subject: Fwd: Production errors and slowdowns — seeing 503s in batching job

Marissa / Monica,

Forwarding Zenith's report — they see 503 spikes and sustained latency during their batch run. Initial read: logs point to sudden enforcement of a lower burst window on the shared token-bucket for this customer tier. Not yet confirmed.

Telemetry note: cluster-hosted relay saw a 3.2x jump in queued requests for the grpc-proxy around 13:46 PT. I pulled a snapshot of the current rate policy and attached it (rate_policy_snapshot_20270921.json).

Immediate asks:
- Monica: can you validate whether a global policy change or a deploy touched the token-bucket config around 13:30–14:00 PT?
- Vanessa: can you standby for a possible temporary whitelist or policy rollback authorization?
- Marissa: heads-up this may require exec visibility if Zenith requests credits — they have enterprise SLA.

I'll keep Zenith in the loop with a short status update.

Thanks,
Mateo
Product Reliability

Subject: Re: Fwd: Production errors and slowdowns — seeing 503s in batching job

On Tue, Sep 21, 2027 at 2:18 PM Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com> wrote:
> Forwarding Zenith's report — they see 503 spikes and sustained latency during their batch run. Initial read: logs point to sudden enforcement of a lower burst window on the shared token-bucket for this customer tier. Not yet confirmed.

Following up with infra: we had a scheduled change this morning to tighten burst windows on the default policy to prevent a noisy neighbor issue after a large customer onboarding last week. That change targeted non-enterprise tenants, but a metric mislabeling during rollforward caused the policy to be applied to the "enterprise_reserve" bucket for traffic coming from the us-west-2 serving plane.

Karthik — can you verify the rollback plan? If this is accurate, we should restore previous burst window and re-run the affected batch. Also need a timeline for a safe rollback and whether it requires an infra restart.

Monica
SRE
Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, mateo_alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2027 15:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Production errors and slowdowns — seeing 503s in batching job

We validated: the deploy pipeline introduced a config flag that toggles "shared_burst_limit" for the token-bucket. A bad selector caused the flag to evaluate true for customers with the enterprise tag when traffic originated from the us-west-2 routing plane. That reduced the burst window from 1.2s -> 120ms at the proxy layer which explains the sequential 503s under bursty batch fanout.

Mitigation applied at 15:00 PT:
- Rolled back the flag via feature-gate (no restart).
- Temporarily increased the enterprise token-bucket capacity for Zenith's customer-id as a whitelist until the next maintenance window.
- Created INF-7621 to track root cause and a postmortem.

Next steps:
1) Postmortem with infra + release team to stop selector leaks.
2) Review release gating and add an integration test that simulates enterprise traffic from each routing plane.
3) Provide Zenith an SLA credit estimate if they request it.

Karthik
Infra Engineering
Redwood

From: mateo_alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Sara Patel <sara.patel@zenithhealth.com>, Alex Reed <alex.reed@zenithhealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2027 16:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production errors and slowdowns — seeing 503s in batching job

Sara / Alex — thanks for the traces, and sorry for the disruption. Quick summary and immediate actions we took:

What happened:
- A release this morning unintentionally tightened the shared burst window on the token-bucket selector used by our us-west-2 plane.
- Due to a selector misrouting, that policy applied to some enterprise traffic (including Zenith) which reduced the proxy burst allowance (~1.2s -> ~120ms), causing queued requests to be dropped and return 503s during Zenith's batch fanout.

What we did:
- We rolled back the feature flag at 15:00 PT and restored the prior burst window.
- Whitelisted Zenith's customer-id for enterprise token capacity until the full patch is deployed.
- Opened ticket INF-7621 (link below) and attached the request traces you provided.

Next steps we will take within 48 hours:
- Postmortem and release pipeline hardening; integration test coverage for per-plane selectors.
- Provide you with a timeline for an automated fix and proposed SLA credit; a customer success rep will follow up on credit details.

Attachments: sla_credit_request.docx (if you'd like a formal request template)

We understand the batch job timing is critical — if you prefer, I can schedule a 30-minute bridge this afternoon to walk through the mitigations and confirm replay of the affected run.

—Mateo
Product Reliability
Redwood Inference

- We've scheduled a postmortem and will share an initial write-up by EOD tomorrow.

- Working with our infra team to add a gating test and a publish checklist so selectors are validated before rollouts.

If you'd like exec-level confirmation of the credit, I can loop in our Head of Customer Success. We value Zenith's partnership and want to ensure we make this right.

Thanks for your patience, and please ping me directly if your next nightly run needs coordination.

—Marissa
